title: Extend missing GitHub operations through ephemeral Actions and API calls
summary: When the connected GitHub tool lacks a repository operation, extend the reachable GitHub capability without polluting the main branch: prefer the native connector first, then use an ephemeral branch-scoped GitHub Actions workflow with least-privilege GITHUB_TOKEN permissions and gh api REST/GraphQL calls, make the operation idempotent where possible, verify the real remote effect, and remove or neutralize the helper branch/workflow afterward.

intents: perform a GitHub repository operation missing from the connected GitHub tool
extend GitHub automation with REST or GraphQL without adding permanent helper code to main
use a temporary GitHub Actions bridge for a repository-scoped API mutation
constraints: Use a native connected GitHub action whenever one exists and fits the operation; this Skill is a fallback for a concrete capability gap.
Do not use this pattern to bypass user authorization, repository permissions, platform consent, or an unavailable security-sensitive scope.
Use the workflow GITHUB_TOKEN with the narrowest permissions required by the target API. Do not persist personal access tokens or unrelated secrets.
For destructive or externally visible mutations, require the same explicit user authorization that would be required for a native connector action.
Design retries to be idempotent where possible by reading current remote state or checking a stable identity before mutating.
The temporary workflow must not be merged into main. After verified completion, delete the helper branch when supported or reset it to the current default-branch head.
If the repository token cannot obtain the required endpoint or permission, fail explicitly instead of escalating credentials or inventing success.

procedure.instruction: Inspect the available connected GitHub actions and identify the exact missing operation. If a native action supports it, stop and use that action instead.
Map the missing operation to the smallest GitHub REST or GraphQL request, required repository permission, stable target identity, idempotency check, and postcondition that will prove success.

Create a temporary branch from the current default-branch head and add one branch-scoped workflow that runs only for the helper path. Give GITHUB_TOKEN only the permissions required by the planned API call and keep the payload/helper code off main.
Run the operation through gh api using REST or GraphQL. Read remote state first when needed to prevent duplicate effects, and surface API/permission failures as failures.

Verify the real GitHub-side postcondition using workflow output and, when useful, a follow-up API read. A green workflow alone is not proof if the requested remote resource or state cannot be resolved.
After verification, remove the temporary branch if ref deletion is available; otherwise reset that branch to the current default-branch head. Confirm the helper workflow was never merged into main.
Record the operation type, workflow run, verified remote resource/state, and cleanup result as durable task evidence so later uses can strengthen or invalidate this Skill.
